title: [Bug]: claude-code skill presents a throwaway git worktree as a safe place for --dangerously-skip-permissions
body:
## Bug Description

The bundled `claude-code` skill documents `--dangerously-skip-permissions` as an explicit opt-in, which is right. But it names a git worktree as one of the two places where that opt-in is acceptable. On `main` `69f73ec5f11f5a945cc864f29c4e2ad2307eaec3`, `skills/autonomous-ai-agents/claude-code/SKILL.md`:

- L121, *Opt-in: --dangerously-skip-permissions*: "Acceptable only in a throwaway worktree or isolated container."
- L286, flag table: "Throwaway worktree / isolated container only"

Anthropic's docs list three boundaries for this flag, and a worktree is not one of them:

- [Sandbox environments](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sandbox-environments): the documented choices for bypass mode are a container, VM, or whole-process sandbox runtime, with a non-root user. Restricting only the built-in Bash tool does not cover the session's file tools, MCP servers, and hooks.
- [Worktrees](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/worktrees): these separate edit locations, not all process access. The documented worktree checks do not follow every destination a shell command writes, and worktrees use shared Git metadata.
- [Dev containers](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/devcontainer): container access still includes whatever is mounted or stored inside it; bypass mode does not prevent a malicious project from exporting that accessible data. Containers therefore do not justify an absolute isolation claim.

Following this wording can lead an agent to treat `claude -w <name>` as containment for a no-prompt session. The worktree itself adds no filesystem, network, or credential boundary; any such restriction must come from a separately configured permission or runtime boundary.

The sentence came in with #114781 (the fix for #113447, whose report suggested "throwaway worktree, isolated container"). That change's direction, bypass as an explicit opt-in, is right; only the worktree premise is wrong. This is separate from #136926 / #136937, which fix the timed `Enter` on the trust dialog and explicitly leave this section unchanged.

This is a documentation defect. It does not claim that a particular run escaped anything.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Read `skills/autonomous-ai-agents/claude-code/SKILL.md` L119–121 and L286 on `main`.
2. Compare them with the three Anthropic pages above.
3. To check the proposed fix, save the diff under *Proposed Fix* as `bypass-worktree.patch` in a checkout of `69f73ec5` and run `git apply bypass-worktree.patch`. In a provisioned checkout, use the repository runner: `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/skills/test_skill_document_contracts.py -- -q -k claude`. The author checks reported below used the smaller fixture, not that full-checkout command: the new test passed with the diff and failed with only the `SKILL.md` hunks reverted.

## Expected Behavior

Bypass stays a documented opt-in. It is acceptable only when explicitly requested, with the whole Claude Code process inside a container, a VM or the sandbox runtime, run as a non-root user, and with known reach (files, network, credentials). A worktree, like the built-in Bash sandbox on its own, is not described as such a boundary.

Unchanged: the default permission-prompt flow, the `acceptEdits` paragraph (its "dedicated worktree" is about where edits land, which is a fair use of a worktree), and the warning-dialog steps.

## Actual Behavior

The skill tells the agent that a throwaway worktree is enough for a session with no permission prompts.

## Affected Component

Skills: bundled `claude-code` skill documentation (`SKILL.md` and its generated docs page).

## Debug Report

Not applicable. This is a documentation-only defect with no runtime involved.

## Operating System / Python / Hermes Version

Not runtime-specific. Inspected `main` `69f73ec5f11f5a945cc864f29c4e2ad2307eaec3`. All three relevant files were rechecked at main `3f2b1722b1e15b12e9ca199a19cb04012493288a` and match that snapshot. The test was run on Linux with Python 3.12.3 and pytest 9.1.1.

## Proposed Fix

Two sentences in `SKILL.md`, a focused contract test, and the skill page regenerated with `website/scripts/generate-skill-docs.py`.

What I ran (author checks): the new test fails on `main` and passes with the diff, and reverting either `SKILL.md` hunk alone makes it fail again. Rendering `main`'s `SKILL.md` with the generator's own `render_skill_page` reproduces `main`'s page byte for byte, and the page in the diff was rendered the same way. The test ran on a minimal copy (the exact test file plus `parse_frontmatter`, `-k claude`), not the full suite. The same diff also applies cleanly on top of #136937's head; the hunks don't overlap.

````diff
--- a/skills/autonomous-ai-agents/claude-code/SKILL.md
+++ b/skills/autonomous-ai-agents/claude-code/SKILL.md
@@ -118,7 +118,7 @@
 
 ### Opt-in: --dangerously-skip-permissions (isolated environments only)
 
-This disables permission prompts for the whole run — grants filesystem, shell, and network access with no prompts. Acceptable only in a throwaway worktree or isolated container.
+This disables permission prompts for the whole run — grants filesystem, shell, and network access with no prompts. Use it only when bypass was explicitly requested, and only with the whole Claude Code process inside an isolation boundary — a container, a VM, or the [sandbox runtime](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sandbox-environments#sandbox-runtime) — run as a non-root user, where you know which files, network and credentials the session can reach. A git worktree (including `claude -w`) isolates file edits only; it is not a filesystem, network or credential sandbox. Neither is the built-in Bash sandbox (`/sandbox`) on its own: file tools, MCP servers and hooks still run on the host. Even in a container, whatever is mounted or stored there — including Claude Code's own login in `~/.claude` — stays reachable.
 ```
 ❯ 1. No, exit                    ← DEFAULT (safe choice)
   2. Yes, I accept
@@ -283,7 +283,7 @@
 ### Permission & Safety
 | Flag | Effect |
 |------|--------|
-| `--dangerously-skip-permissions` | Opt-in only: disables ALL permission prompts (file writes, bash, network). Throwaway worktree / isolated container only — see "Opt-in" above |
+| `--dangerously-skip-permissions` | Opt-in only: disables ALL permission prompts (file writes, bash, network). Container, VM or sandbox runtime only; a worktree is not a sandbox — see "Opt-in" above |
 | `--allow-dangerously-skip-permissions` | Enable bypass as an *option* without enabling it by default |
 | `--permission-mode <mode>` | `default`, `acceptEdits`, `plan`, `auto`, `dontAsk`, `bypassPermissions` |
 | `--allowedTools <tools...>` | Whitelist specific tools (comma or space-separated) |
--- a/tests/skills/test_skill_document_contracts.py
+++ b/tests/skills/test_skill_document_contracts.py
@@ -118,3 +118,13 @@
 def test_optional_skill_availability_on_windows():
     assert skill_matches_platform(_document(QUESTIONNAIRE)[0])
     assert not skill_matches_platform(_document(DARWINIAN)[0])
+
+
+def test_claude_code_bypass_is_not_scoped_to_a_worktree():
+    # A git worktree isolates file edits, not the filesystem, network or credentials, so it
+    # must not be offered as the place where the permission bypass is safe; the boundaries
+    # Anthropic documents for bypass are a container, a VM or the sandbox runtime.
+    _, body = _document("skills/autonomous-ai-agents/claude-code")
+    assert "it is not a filesystem, network or credential sandbox" in body
+    assert "sandbox runtime" in body
+    assert not re.search(r"throwaway worktree", body, re.IGNORECASE)
--- a/website/docs/user-guide/skills/bundled/autonomous-ai-agents/autonomous-ai-agents-claude-code.md
+++ b/website/docs/user-guide/skills/bundled/autonomous-ai-agents/autonomous-ai-agents-claude-code.md
@@ -136,7 +136,7 @@
 
 ### Opt-in: --dangerously-skip-permissions (isolated environments only)
 
-This disables permission prompts for the whole run — grants filesystem, shell, and network access with no prompts. Acceptable only in a throwaway worktree or isolated container.
+This disables permission prompts for the whole run — grants filesystem, shell, and network access with no prompts. Use it only when bypass was explicitly requested, and only with the whole Claude Code process inside an isolation boundary — a container, a VM, or the [sandbox runtime](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sandbox-environments#sandbox-runtime) — run as a non-root user, where you know which files, network and credentials the session can reach. A git worktree (including `claude -w`) isolates file edits only; it is not a filesystem, network or credential sandbox. Neither is the built-in Bash sandbox (`/sandbox`) on its own: file tools, MCP servers and hooks still run on the host. Even in a container, whatever is mounted or stored there — including Claude Code's own login in `~/.claude` — stays reachable.
 ```
 ❯ 1. No, exit                    ← DEFAULT (safe choice)
   2. Yes, I accept
@@ -301,7 +301,7 @@
 ### Permission & Safety
 | Flag | Effect |
 |------|--------|
-| `--dangerously-skip-permissions` | Opt-in only: disables ALL permission prompts (file writes, bash, network). Throwaway worktree / isolated container only — see "Opt-in" above |
+| `--dangerously-skip-permissions` | Opt-in only: disables ALL permission prompts (file writes, bash, network). Container, VM or sandbox runtime only; a worktree is not a sandbox — see "Opt-in" above |
 | `--allow-dangerously-skip-permissions` | Enable bypass as an *option* without enabling it by default |
 | `--permission-mode <mode>` | `default`, `acceptEdits`, `plan`, `auto`, `dontAsk`, `bypassPermissions` |
 | `--allowedTools <tools...>` | Whitelist specific tools (comma or space-separated) |
````
